summary:
H.R. 7198, the "Prove It Act of 2024," amends Chapter 6 of Title 5, United States Code, to impose additional analytical and procedural requirements on federal agencies for regulatory actions impacting small entities.

Section 2 amends 5 U.S.C. § 603(b) to require that initial regulatory flexibility analyses include, where feasible, reasonably foreseeable potential indirect costs on small entities that conduct business with directly regulated entities, are regulated by other governmental entities as a result of the rule, or are subject to other agency rules as a result of the rule. It also amends 5 U.S.C. § 605(b) to require that an agency publish its certification that a proposed rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities not later than 10 days after completing the certification.

Section 2 further enacts new 5 U.S.C. § 605A, establishing a petition process for small entities to request the Chief Counsel for Advocacy of the Small Business Administration to review an agency's § 605(b) certification. The Chief Counsel must conduct a prima facie review within 10 days of receipt. If further review is warranted, the Chief Counsel must conduct a full review within 30 days, convening a meeting with the petitioner, the promulgating agency, and the Administrator of the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs. If the Chief Counsel determines the rule will have a significant economic impact, the agency must perform initial and final regulatory flexibility analyses under §§ 603 and 604. If an agency fails to attend the meeting or assist in the review, the final rule shall not apply to small entities. The certification is considered final agency action for purposes of judicial review under Chapter 7 upon the Chief Counsel's determination to close the matter or publish the full review results.

Section 3 amends 5 U.S.C. § 609 to require agency heads to publish guidance documents and accept public comments on regulations.gov for rules likely to have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.

Section 4 amends 5 U.S.C. § 610 to require that periodic reviews of rules consider indirect costs identified in § 603(b)(6) and any other indirect costs arising during the 10-year review period. It adds subsection (d), providing that if an agency fails to conduct the required 10-year review, the rule ceases to be effective. The agency must publish a Federal Register notice soliciting comments for reinstatement. If reinstated, the agency has 180 days to complete the review, after which the rule is reinstated notwithstanding the notice-and-comment procedures of 5 U.S.C. § 553. This amendment applies to final rules issued during the 5-year period preceding enactment or on or after the date of enactment.
